chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ali ibn Al-No'man, from Abdullah ibn Muskaan, from Abdul Raheem Al-Qaseer who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'The people are appalled when we say that the people turned apostate.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abdul Raheem, the people returned to the ways of ignorance after the passing away of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The Helpers (Al-Ansar) isolated themselves, but their isolation was not in goodness. They began pledging allegiance to Sa'd while reciting the poetry of ignorance: O Sa'd, you are the hoped-for one, and your hair is combed, and your stud camel is the one with the red spot.'

key_terms.الْمُرَجَّمُ: The one with the red spot (referring to a camel)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq mean when he said the people 'returned to the ways of ignorance' after the Prophet's death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the post-Prophetic 'apostasy' was essentially a regression to pre-Islamic tribalism (jahiliyyah) rather than a total abandonment of faith, specifically highlighting the Ansar's political isolation and their pledge to Sa'd. This event underscores the Shia scholarly view that the crisis was one of leadership legitimacy and tribal loyalty, where the Ansar's poetic declaration of Sa'd as 'the one to be hoped for' reflected their desire for a leader from their own ranks, mirroring the customs of the Jahiliyyah era.
